rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation for Hell reflects foreknown free choices: people first receive human nature and covenant capacities, then fail to use them, whereupon God seals those powers and gives a final hellward nature; this is not sheer compulsion.
rows.anchor: bidâyet-i hilkatlerinde ahsen-i takvîm üzere yaratılmış şuur fıtratını taahhüd etmiş iken sonra esfel-i sâfilîne düşmüş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have compelled these people to fulfill their covenant or not created them, but why He did not is solely His unanswerable will; nothing obligates or constrains Him.
rows.anchor: Meşiyyete müdahale olunamaz, o ne mecburdur ne de mes’ul; لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To show there is no sheer compulsion, Elmalılı stresses that they possess hearts, eyes, and ears but fail to use these God-given human capacities to understand, see, and hear rightly.
rows.anchor: Bunların kalbleri vardır. Kendilerine duyacak kalb verilmemiş, mîsâk-ı fıtrata rabt olunmamış değillerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are more astray than cattle because animals follow their nature, pursue available benefits and avoid harms, while humans corrupt a nature intended for higher felicity and fall into eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: en‘âm, fıtrat ve garîzelerinden sapmaz, seçebilecekleri kadar menfaat ve mazarratlarını seçer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truly heedless have senses but no consciousness: they do not grasp their primordial testimony or heed either inward reflection or outward signs, scripture, and God's speech.
rows.anchor: Fıtratlarındaki taahhüdü duymazlar, kendi dikkatleriyle, fıkh-ı nefsleriyle[^19] duymadıkları gibi âfâktan gözlerine sokulan âyât ve kitabın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one and incomparable, not a merely numerical unity that could have a partner; He is self-sufficient and gathers all attributes of perfection.
rows.anchor: Allah zâtında birdir, ehaddır ve ism-i zâtı bir Allah’tır. Fakat vâhid-i adedî gibi şerîk ü nazîri bulunabilecek fakir bir vahdetle değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The multiplicity of God's names and attributes does not entail multiplicity in His essence; His names point to divine attributes of supreme perfection.
rows.anchor: sıfât u esmânın kesreti zât ve müsemmânın ta‘addüd ve kesretini iktizâ etmeyeceğinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic plural in divine speech signals the collected grandeur of God's essence, attributes, and names while affirming His unity.
rows.anchor: hitâbât-ı ilâhiyede vârid olan انا، شهدنا، ذرأنا gibi cem‘-i azamet, bu zât ve sıfât ve esmânın mertebe-i cem‘iyyetindeki azamet ü kibriyâyı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should call upon, remember, and describe God by His most beautiful names.
rows.anchor: o esmâ-i hüsnâ, o en güzel isimler ile dua, zikr ediniz veya O’nu bunlarla tavsif ve yâd ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı warns against names that carry a false or bad implication or fail to express utmost perfection, illustrating this with Bedouin invocations such as “Abā al-Makārim” and “Abyad al-Wajh.”
rows.anchor: bedevîlerin ،يَا أَبَا الْمَكَارِم، يَا أَبـْيَضَ الْوَجْهِ يَا نجي demeleri gibi sû’-i îhâmdan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād includes rejecting al-Raḥmān or objecting to God's majestic names, applying names reserved for God to others, and deriving idol names al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā from Allah and al-ʿAzīz; believers should leave such people to their recompense.
rows.anchor: Allah’a mahsus olan esmâ-i hüsnâyı Allah’ın gayrısına aynen ıtlak, yahut Arap müşriklerinin putlarına “Allah” isminden te’nîs ile اَل َّلات ve “el-Azîz” isminden اَلْعُ َّزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those God created is a virtuous community that guides by truth and administers justice accordingly; following its consensus is guidance.
rows.anchor: hakka sarılarak rehberlik ederler ve bihakkın icrâ-yı adalet eylerler. Binâen‘aleyh bunların icmâ‘ına ittibâ‘hidâyettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A community keeps a blessing God bestowed until it changes what was within itself, especially the primordial covenant and the good morals and deeds that enabled it to receive that blessing.
rows.anchor: o nimete nâil oldukları zaman nefislerinde ona vesile olan mîsâk-ı fıtratı[^2] ve ahlâk ve a‘mâl-i haseneyi kendileri tağyir edinceye kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's custom ties the alteration of blessings originally given through inward causes to inward causes again, so human responsibility follows from the change.
rows.anchor: Âdet-i ilâhiye enfüsî esbâb ile verdiği nimetin tağyîrini de yine esbâb-ı enfüsiyeye rabt etmiştir ki mes’ûliyyet-i beşeriye de buna terettüb eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears and knows everyone's inward state, words, and deeds, and judges them accordingly.
rows.anchor: Allah muhakkak Semî‘ve Alîm’dir. Herkesin enfüsiyyâtını, kavl ü fiilini bilir ve ona göre muâhaze eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessings given or removed directly, without following inward causes such as will, faith, morals, or deeds, fall outside this principle.
rows.anchor: akl u irade, küfr ü iman, ahlâk u amel gibi esbâb-ı enfüsiyeye müterettib olmayarak doğrudan doğru verilip alınan nimetler bu mevzûdan hâriçtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward causes matter here chiefly through whether people recognize the divine signs that reveal blessing or calamity; an individual breaks the natural covenant by refusing to hear and recognize proofs of truth, bringing a change in blessing.
rows.anchor: Bir nefsin ahd-i fıtratı bozması ve [2420] kendine vârid olan delâil ve emârât-ı hakkı duymak ve tanımak istememesi elindeki nimetin tegayyürüne sebep olacağı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A community also changes its inward condition when it refuses to hear or recognize truthful guides who convey divine rulings, thereby bringing a change in its blessing.
rows.anchor: kendilerine ahkâm-ı ilâhiyeyi tebliğ eden hak rehberlerini duymak ve tanımak istememesi nefs-i ictimâ‘îlerinde öyle[^3] bir bozukluktur ki ellerindeki nimetin tağyîrine sebep olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is from the people's own kind, a human rather than an angel, with known Arab, Qurayshi, Meccan origins.
rows.anchor: bir Resul ki kendinizden kendi cinsinizden, melek değil beşerden, aslı ve nesebi mâlum Arabî, Kureşî, ehl-i Harem’den

rows.speaker: tefsirler
rows.claim: One reported explanation says that even the believers' hardship deeply pains the Messenger, not merely their punishment.
rows.anchor: Yani azab görmeniz şöyle dursun zahmet çekmeniz bile onu son derece müteessir eder

rows.speaker: tefsirler
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says that, by human nature, whatever troubles the believers troubles him too.
rows.anchor: Yahut sizi sıkan, zorunuza giden şeyler hasbe’l-beşeriyye onu da müteessir eder

rows.speaker: İbn Kuşeyrî
rows.claim: Ibn Qushayri's preferred parsing treats “aziz” and “whatever distresses you is against him” as two separate adjectives; this yields the added sense that his great honor makes him feel all his people's grief.
rows.anchor: “azîz” bir sıfat, عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ de diğer bir sıfattır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some muṣḥafs place a jim pause after “aziz,” marking the additional sense of the preferred parsing.
rows.anchor: bazı mushaflarda “azîz” üzerine bir “cim” secâvendi konulmuştur ki bunda daha fazla bir mâna vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is ardently concerned for the believers' guidance, righteousness, benefit, and salvation, striving to lead them to the highest felicity and Paradise.
rows.anchor: Üzerinize toz kondurmak istemediği gibi sizi aksâyı saadet ve selâmete çıkarmak, cennet ve rıdvâna erdirmek için bütün hırsıyla uğraşır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His compassion extends to all believers, whatever their tribe, rather than only Quraysh, Arabs, or a particular people.
rows.anchor: bütün mü’minleredir ki raûfdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is deeply merciful by God-given nature and pities even sinners.
rows.anchor: Fıtraten min-tarafillah pek ziyade[^3] merhametlidir. Günahkârlara bile acır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic obligations, especially the commands about disavowal, repentance, and jihad in this surah, should not feel burdensome because they manifest great compassion for believers against disbelief and hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: Bütün bunlar küfr ü nifâkın zarar ve şeâmetine karşı ale’l-umûm mü’minlere[^4] gayet büyük bir re’fet ve şefkatin tecelliyâtıdır

rows.speaker: Hasan b. el-Fazl
rows.claim: Hasan b. al-Faḍl says God joined two of His names for no prophet other than Muhammad, calling him Raʾūf and Raḥīm, as God also describes Himself.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ hiçbir peygambere esmâsından iki ismi cem‘etmedi, ancak Peygamberimiz hakkında بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ buyurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This naming is a great divine honor; not all beautiful names are exclusive to God, since the Prophet embodies divine ethics and is merciful to believers, while his religion and law are mercy for them.
rows.anchor: Resûlüne pek büyük bir tekrîm-i ilâhî vardır. Bundan anlaşılır ki esmâ-i hüsnâ-yı ilâhiyenin hepsi “Allah”, “er-Rahman”, “er-Rab” isimleri gibi esmâ-i muhtassadan değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and righteous deeds lead believers, through their Lord, to their intended destination in the gardens of bliss, with rivers flowing beneath them.
rows.anchor: bunları kendilerinin Rabbi olan o Rabb-i celîl imanları sebebiyle dosdoğru muradlarına erdirecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's residents continually glorify God because, freed from mortal anxiety and having reached certainty and divine favor, they have no other aim or request.
rows.anchor: artık başka bir talep ve maksatları kalmamış bulunacağından duaları Allah’a hep böyle arz-ı tesbih ve tenzih

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their greetings from God and the angels and to one another are an unqualified, permanent safety from every disliked thing, not a vague or temporary wish.
rows.anchor: hep selâm bilâ kayd ü şart selâmet, bütün mekrûhâttan mutlak ve dâimî bir selâmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayers end in praise of God as Lord of the worlds, recalling al-Fatiha's opening; praise is the special honor due to the giver and expresses joy in appreciating blessing.
rows.anchor: “Elhamdü lillâhi Rabbi’l-âlemîn” diye Allah’a hamd ü şükrandır ki Fâtiha’nın evvelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's bliss culminates in the infinite perfection of God's approval: residents will recognize the giver rather than forget or disdain blessings, and honoring God will remain their greatest pleasure despite having no need or worship obligation.
rows.anchor: ehl-i cennet en büyük lezzet ve ibtihâcın kibriyâ-yı Hakk’ı iclâl ve tekrimde bulunduğunu görerek Allah’a duadan ayrılmayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a worldly likeness of this joy: the ignorant treat it as a burden and pray only under pressure, while the gnostics experience it as delight and spiritual ascent.
rows.anchor: Ârifler ise bunu büyük bir zevk ve mi‘râc bilirler.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that prayer was made the coolness of his eyes and that prayer is the believer's ascension.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm [^3] وَجُعِلَتْ قـُ َّرةُ عَيْنِي فِي ال َّصلاَةِ ve [^4] اَل َّصلَوةُ مِعْرَاجُ الْمُؤْمِنِ buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the people of Paradise greet one another with peace, Muslims end each prayer and remembrance with a Fatiha to share in that taste of Paradise.
rows.anchor: ehl-i İslâm her dua ve tezkirlerinin sonunda bir Fâtiha okurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People die in the spiritual condition formed by their habitual life and will be resurrected as they died.
rows.anchor: insanlar dünyada itiyad ettikleri yaşayış [2682] hâlet-i rûhiyesiyle ölecekler ve öldükleri gibi haşrolunacaklardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those content with worldly life and heedless of God's signs meet painful Hell after death, while believers who are grateful arrive in peace, saying praise belongs to God.
rows.anchor: ehl-i iman ve şükran, selâm ü selâmetle ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ diyeceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı asks whether the disbelievers deny God's promise and tauntingly demand that punishment come at once, even stones falling on them.
rows.anchor: “hani Allah öyle kādir de kâfirlere, âsîlere azâbını neye tehir ediyor? Şimdiden hesâbımızı görüverse ya, başımıza taşlar yağdırıverse ya!...” mı diyorlar?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he asks whether afflicted people lose patience and wish that God would take their lives.
rows.anchor: Veya dünyada başlarına bir sıkıntı geliverirse sabredemeyip “Allah canımızı alsa” mı diyorlar?
